plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their bidding behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks losses if you win, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $6, I should bid exactly $6 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and pay a fair price when I do win.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing a profitable auction. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, and since this is a one-shot game, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. Bidding above my value risks negative profit if I win at a price above my valuation; bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions. With a value of $45, I should bid exactly $45 to ensure optimal outcomes in all scenarios.
